messages.author: f806781d102fe0ab
messages.subject: Re: Table with checkboxes?
parts:
Attaching a modified version. It's not all the way there, but it's a lot closer.

If you find yourself with nested reactive functions, that's generally a code smell. It's great when reactive functions refer to each other:

a <- reactive(function() {...})
b <- reactivePlot(function() { a(); ... })

but not so much when the are actually defined one within the other:

a <- reactive(function() {
  b <- reactivePlot(function() {...})
})

Not saying there is *never* occasion to do that, but I can't think of a scenario where you would.

messages.author: 757f82d0e9848db8
messages.subject: Re: Table with checkboxes?
parts:
That's odd - maybe I uploaded an incomplete version... Try the one I've attached here.

As far as choosing columns, I've actually implemented something similar using a multiple selectInput. Here's roughly how I did it (very partial code):

global:

col_list <- as.list(colnames(myData))

ui:

selectInput("myCols", "Select data columns:", col_list)

server:

myData2 <- reactive(function(){
    foo <- myData[,input$myCols]
    return(foo)
    }
)
